idiom_name: one-line class method / getter checked by implements
implementation_notes: TypeScript writes the same one-liner as JavaScript - cancel(id: OrderID): CancelResult { return this.repo.cancel(id); } - and adds the guardrail the pattern wants: an implements clause checks that the class declares every interface member with a compatible signature, but it never generates members and does not flow the interface's parameter types into the class body. Nothing in the compiler replaces the delegation, so each forwarder is explicit and must be kept in sync by the implementer; decorators, mixins and declaration merging can add members at runtime or in the type space, but they bypass the named, checkable surface that makes the one-liner worth writing.
pitfalls: implements is only a check: it does not create members, does not carry the interface's parameter types into the class (an unannotated parameter becomes any), and an optional interface property still does not exist on the class.
A forwarding getter satisfies a property-typed interface member but nothing caches it: each access runs the delegate, which is easy to forget when the member is read as if it were a field.
Types are erased and structural, so a forwarder nothing requires is never flagged as unused - dead one-liners survive type checking until a lint rule catches them.
